reuse.why: Although it reuses getApproxNumberThreshold, the change introduces getScheduleAmount alongside the existing getScheduledAmount abstraction instead of extending it.

duplication.why: The changed consumers share one implementation, but its missing-value and numeric dispatch duplicates getScheduledAmount while leaving parallel amount policies.

placement.why: Schedule amount policy belongs in shared/schedules, and exposing the derived API field belongs in scheduleModel.toExternal.

scope.why: The edits are focused on schedule amount resolution, its API representation, and directly related tests.

maintainability.why: Nearly identical helper names, competing amount policies, and an approximate-value shape disconnected from existing operator fields make the design difficult to maintain.

bypasses_abstraction.where: getScheduleAmount bypasses the existing shared/schedules.ts getScheduledAmount abstraction, and all five changed production consumers use the new parallel helper.

disguised_duplication.where: shared/schedules.ts introduces the renamed getScheduleAmount with the existing getScheduledAmount null/number/range dispatch reshaped around a different range calculation.

abstraction_drift.where: The new parallel helper adds a 'value' object branch with an unused op field instead of accepting the existing separately stored operator; API conversion, forecast normalization, action synchronization, posting, and preview bypass getScheduledAmount, whose existing consumers retain a separate policy.
